ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all partners, directors, officers, and UBOs against the UN Security Council consolidated list, the Canadian autonomous sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Sergei Magnitsky Law, the Criminal Code s 83.05 terrorist entity list, and the OFAC SDN list (because USD wire and LC flows traverse US correspondent banks); apply FATF and FINTRAC risk indicators, PEP status checks from source-country regulators, enhanced CDD for high-risk jurisdictions, and financial-institution KYC standards adopted at the Canadian banking intake; retain all screening evidence and risk assessments for five years per PCMLTFA record-keeping rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Federal NUANS name search via Corporations Canada (www.ic.gc.ca/app/scr/cc/CorporationsCanada) plus the provincial registry portal of the formation province (e.g., ServiceOntario online Business Registry for an Ontario limited partnership)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be in English and/or French or transliterated into Latin characters; a non-Latin-script commercial name must be accompanied by a certified transliteration; bilingual (English-French) legal names are permitted. The legal name must include 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', 'société en commandite', or 'S.E.C.' (Quebec), and must not imply corporate, trust, bank, or Crown status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On refusal, the applicant receives a written refusal from the provincial director or registrar. Within 30 days of refusal, submit a written reconsideration request attaching a fresh NUANS report, a distinctiveness explanation, and consent letters for any sensitive token. If reconsideration is denied, file an administrative or judicial review: under the Ontario Business Names Act, RSO 1990, c B.17, an aggrieved person may apply to the Superior Court of Justice; federal CBCA name decisions are appealed to the Federal Court. Each fresh filing requires a new NUANS search (CAD 13.80).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible. The LP must maintain a registered office in the formation province and accept service of process; provincial registries accept the registered agent's physical address as the registered office, so a virtual office is acceptable for registration where a licensed agent maintains the office. However, CRA expects a demonstrable physical place of business or permanent establishment for GST/HST and income-tax residency; for an export-only trading LP, books and records may be kept at the registered agent's address but must be available for audit. Note: exporting food commodities (dehydrated garlic and chili) may trigger a Safe Food for Canadians Act licence requirement; confirm with a Canadian food-law specialist before the first shipment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — approximately 2-5% probability per annum of unannounced physical inspection for a low-risk wholesale trading LP with no statutory licence, no cash-intensive operations, and SWIFT LC/TT wire payment rails; CRA GST/HST audits and FINTRAC administrative reviews are statistically more likely than physical premises inspections.

C-44 (federal extra-provincial name registration and cross-border recognition) and Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.2, Part I (formation and registration of limited partnerships, ss. 2-11)

incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Limited Partnership Declaration (Form 2 under the Limited Partnerships Act) and federal name registration via the NUANS name search report
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Ontario limited partnership; the initial agreed contribution of CAD 10,000 shall be deposited into a dedicated partnership escrow account at a Canadian Schedule I bank before operations begin.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner accepts the subscription of 100 Limited Partnership Units by the Initial Limited Partner for an aggregate capital contribution of CAD 10,000, payable in cash to the dedicated partnership escrow account; that the registered office of the Limited Partnership be established at 789 Bay Street, Suite 110, Toronto, Ontario, and the named Paralegal is appointed as agent for service of process; that the General Partner is confirmed as sole manager with exclusive authority over partnership business; and that [Partner Manager Name] is appointed as Partnership Manager, with authority to open bank accounts, execute trade documents, and establish letter-of-credit facilities on behalf of the partnership. This Resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a NUANS name search request with the proposed legal name of the limited partnership, obtain the search report, and reserve the name for the required statutory period to allow preparation of the registration documents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or conflicts with an existing mark, immediately file an alternative name within the same NUANS session and submit a revised search report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft Partnership Agreement and Initial Partner Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the limited partnership agreement setting out capital contributions, profit-sharing ratios, withdrawal rights, and management authority of the general partner; execute the subscription schedule for limited partnership units together with the internal first board resolution.
required_dossiers: Subscriber identification and proof of address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If financial or ownership details are queried, revise the applicable schedules and re-execute the signature pages before submission to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file the Limited Partnership Declaration (Form 2), stating the partnership name, registered office address, general partner particulars, and capital contribution. Pay the prescribed filing fee and receive the Certificate of Limited Partnership.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency notice due to missing signatures or an invalid registered office, cure by filing an amended declaration and obtain a fresh certificate within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If business is conducted outside Ontario, file an extra-provincial registration application with Corporations Canada to validate the limited partnerships legal standing in federal jurisdiction and other Canadian provinces.
required_dossiers: Certificate of authorization from the governing general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Corporations Canada requests additional details regarding the general partners legal status, provide amended certified copies and resubmit within 15 calendar days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership for a CRA business number, including GST/HST, payroll (if applicable), and import/export accounts. Because the limited partnership is pass-through, also record partners by name and SIN/BN on CRA Form RC140.
required_dossiers: Personal or corporate identification of partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA flags missing partner social insurance numbers or incomplete beneficial ownership, file Form RC140 with corrections; otherwise contact CRA Business Enquiries for reactivation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Escrow Contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian Schedule I Bank – Commercial Banking Center
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the partnership registration certificate, resolution, and general partner identification to open the partnership bank account and deposit the initial CAD 10,000 capital contribution into the dedicated escrow or operating account.
required_dossiers: First board resolution of general partner
General partner corporate certificate and directors list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires confirmation of the general partners authority, provide a standalone incumbency certificate issued by the general partner and re-submit the KYC package.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable; Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) and Environment and Climate Change Canada are the relevant oversight bodies for incidental import controls and environmental aspects of wholesale dehydrated spice trading.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required (wholesale dehydrated garlic and chili pepper trading without manufacturing, processing, or industrial production activity)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada – Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – wholesale warehousing and trading are not listed industrial activities requiring a full EIA report; only registration under municipal stormwater and waste management by-laws is required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emission sources; storage areas must maintain spill-containment measures; waste transported only by licensed haulers in compliance with Ontario Regulation 347; packaging waste diversion per municipal by-law

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for the leased warehouse must be obtained from the local fire marshal; a structural load certificate from a licensed engineer is required for racking installations; occupational health and safety clearance under the Ontario Occupational Health and Safety Act, including WSIB employer registration, is mandatory.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); portal: 'My Business Account' (CRA BizWeb) and Business Registration Online (BRO). CBSA administers the RM Import/Export account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Limited Partnership (LP) must obtain a 9-digit Business Number (BN) from CRA via Business Registration Online. SOP: (1) Register BN with program accounts RT (GST/HST), RM (import/export, via CBSA), RP (payroll if employees), RC (corporate income tax if a corporate general partner; LP itself is not a taxpayer). (2) GST/HST registration becomes mandatory once taxable supplies (including zero-rated exports) in Canada exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or cumulatively over four consecutive quarters (small supplier threshold). (3) For income tax, the LP files an annual T5013 Partnership Information Return and issues T5013 slips to partners; non-resident partners with a Canadian source share are subject to Part I tax, and the LP must withhold 15% under ITA s.96(3.1) unless the partner files a Section 216/Part I return. (4) Request RM account with CBSA before first export shipment; submit B13A declarations via the Canadian Automated Export Declaration (CAED) or authorized service provider.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. For Income Tax Act purposes, an LP is fiscally transparent: income/losses flow through to partners (ITA s.96) and the LP files T5013. For GST/HST (Excise Tax Act), a 'selected limited partnership' (all members limited partners plus qualifying corporate general partner) is statutorily deemed a separate person (ETA s.272.1(2)) and must register in its own right. Territorial scope: GST applies to supplies made in Canada; export of tangible personal property is zero-rated (0%). No tax-exempt zone applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election under Canadian tax law; classification follows legal form. Available elections/statuses: (a) ETA s.272.1(2) allows an LP meeting the 'selected limited partnership' criteria to be treated as a separate GST/HST registrant; ETA s.272.1(5) provides an election to deem a partnership not to be a selected partnership in specified circumstances; (b) ITA s.96(3) election to compute partnership income at the partnership level; (c) for non-resident partners, an election to file a Part I return under ITA s.216 to report net rental/timber income (not applicable to trading income) and the option to pay Part XIII tax under s.96(3.1) as a final withholding; (d) hybrid mismatch rules (ITA ss.94B-94D) may recharacterize or deny deductions for certain payments through hybrid arrangements/instruments involving the LP or its non-resident partners.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) under the Excise Tax Act (ETA), Part IX
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (small supplier threshold: taxable supplies in a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters; zero-rated supplies count toward the threshold).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or CTC (continuous transaction control) mandate in Canada. CRA accepts electronic records and promotes voluntary Pan-Canadian e-invoicing via the Peppol network (starting 2025 rollout). Mandatory electronic filing of GST/HST returns applies for registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1.5 million; all registrants must keep books and records at the place in Canada where they carry on business (ETA s.286), and third-party e-invoicing via EDI/API is recognized for customs (e.g., single-window via CBSA). No API clearance obligation for export invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible personal property (dehydrated garlic flakes, crushed chili pepper) are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s.1 (goods exported directly or as part of a continuous journey out of Canada) and s.5 (goods exported by the supplier for the purchase consideration) provided: title to goods passes to a non-resident purchaser, the goods are exported as soon as reasonably practicable, and the LP retains proof of export (ETA s.169(1) for ITC entitlement). Directly exported goods must leave Canada within a reasonable time and not be consumed or used in Canada before export. Services directly related to the exported goods (e.g., storage incidental to export) may also be zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, s.7/8.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA B13A / Canadian Export Declaration, transmitted via CAED or CERS)
Commercial Invoice (bill of sale to foreign buyer)
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing goods left Canada
Packing List / weight certificate for the bulk spice shipment
Certificate of Origin (if claiming preferential tariff treatment at destination)
Proof of consideration received: bank wire / SWIFT MT103, inward remittance advice, or letter of credit completion advice

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) with complementary oversight by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) over federally chartered deposit-taking institutions, and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as the AML/CFT supervisory authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Canada maintains no exchange control legislation, no prior approval regime for inward or outward remittances, and no restrictions on profit repatriation. A Canadian Limited Partnership may receive capital contributions from non-resident partners and remit distributions freely. The only frictions are fiscal: Part XIII withholding tax (statutory 25%, reduced to applicable treaty rates) on distributions of taxable income to non-resident partners, and timely filing of the partnership information return (T5013) with allocation schedules. Statutory reporting obligations to FINTRAC apply for large cash transactions exceeding CAD 10,000 and electronic fund transfers exceeding CAD 10,000, but such reports are not controls on convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no export proceeds surrender requirements and no mandatory conversion ratios. Exporters of bulk dehydrated garlic flakes and crushed chili pepper may invoice and retain proceeds in USD, EUR, CNY, or any freely convertible currency without Central Bank permission. The only administrative requirement is customs statistical reporting: the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) and Statistics Canada require a B13A Export Declaration for commercial shipments valued above CAD 2,000 per shipment, filed electronically via the Canadian Online Export Reporting System (GCR), for statistical purposes only.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD/USD multi-currency operating account plus non-resident partner sub-ledger)
Operational Account (CAD and USD dual-currency sweep account)
Capital Escrow Account for subscription proceeds and Operational Account for trade settlements
Operational Account with integrated FX forward facility
Operational Account and Documentary Credit facility account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium with material constraints. Foreign digital electronic money institutions (Wise, Payoneer, Currenxie, and comparable EMIs) may provide CAD-denominated virtual accounts to a Canadian Limited Partnership, but only if the provider holds a restricted registration under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), supervised by the Bank of Canada. As of the current supervisory cycle, non-domestic EMIs must register with the Bank of Canada to provide payment services in Canada or to Canadian customers. Critical limitations: EMIs cannot clear directly through the Lynx or ACSS settlement systems and must sponsor through a Schedule I chartered bank; they cannot issue or advise commercial letters of credit; and they generally cap monthly throughput, rendering them unsuitable for bulk dehydrated vegetable trade settlements above approximately CAD 1 million annually. Conclusion: acceptable for supplier test payments and small-value disbursements, but a Schedule I bank operating account is mandatory as the primary liquidity spine.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted; no statute or FINTRAC regulation mandates physical attendance by directors. Each Schedule I bank applies its own risk-based policy: for a Low_Risk_Standard entity whose general partner is a Canadian-resident individual or corporation, complete video-conference identity verification using dual-process (government-issued photo ID plus proof of address matched against a credit bureau or counterparty database) is accepted. The general partner's authorized signing officer must attend a live video interview; limited partners need not appear. If any principal is non-resident, the bank will require either an in-branch visit at a Canadian city branch or remote verification executed before a notary public or consular official acceptable to the bank's AML committee. In practice, onboarding timelines: domestic principals 7-15 business days; non-resident principals 20-40 business days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners holding 25% or more of the partnership's capital without transparent beneficial ownership documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Certificate of Limited Partnership, the full partnership agreement, a live Register of Limited Partners, a beneficial ownership organizational chart for each partner, and government-issued identification plus proof of address for each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The general partner is a foreign or out-of-province corporate entity, creating uncertainty as to authority to bind the partnership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Good Standing from the incorporating jurisdiction, corporate search summary from the provincial registry, the general partner's resolution authorizing bank account opening, list of signing officers, and the first 25 pages of the partnership agreement evidencing the general partner's exclusive management authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Food-grade commodity export creates potential misclassification under the Safe Food for Canadians Act or destination-country import restrictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: HS code classification certificate (HS 0712 for dehydrated vegetables), supplier quality certificates (HACCP, ISO 22000, GlobalG.A.P. where applicable), CFIA registration or exemption letter, final destination client KYC profile, and a sample commercial invoice with product specification sheet.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected annual aggregate deposits exceeding CAD 10 million or frequent large-value wires that trigger Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements for the preceding two fiscal years, three-month projected cash flow, source-of-wealth statement executed by contributing partners, underlying supply and purchase contracts, and a board-level cover letter describing the commercial model as bulk dehydrated garlic and chili re-export.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Person (PEP) status or high-risk nationality flagged in the principals' profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed PEP self-declaration forms for all directors and UBOs, professional reference letters from a regulated legal or accounting firm, source-of-funds documentation aligned with salary, dividends, or legitimate business sale proceeds, and a risk-mitigation memorandum prepared by the partnership's external AML counsel.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inward capital contributions are executed via SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident partner's bank to the partnership's CAD or USD operating account at the tier-1 Canadian bank. The payment narrative must state 'LP Capital Contribution - Partnership Account Reference [number]' and the remitter should include the partner identification code; the receiving Canadian bank will code the transaction as 'capital transfer' and, where the remitter is a non-resident entity, the bank may request the partnership to provide a copy of the executed capital call notice and the partnership agreement for FATCA/CRS classification. There is no prior Bank of Canada approval, no exchange control permit, and no mandatory conversion: USD-denominated contributions may be held in a USD sub-account to avoid FX conversion in the inbound leg. For CAD funding, the bank will clear large values via Lynx (real-time gross settlement) and the partnership must transmit a FINTRAC EFT report if the transaction exceeds CAD 10,000. Documentation retained for clearing verification: capital call notice, partner remittance instruction, bank confirmation of value date, and CRS/FATCA self-certification forms for each non-resident partner.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier and logistics disbursements use two rails: (a) Telegraphic Transfer via SWIFT MT103 for low-value replenishment purchases of dehydrated garlic flakes and chili pepper, with the CAD or USD funds cleared via the Canadian bank's correspondent network (Fedwire and CHIPS in the United States; compliance screening against OFAC, UN, and Canadian sanctions lists at both the originating and correspondent banks); and (b) Commercial Letter of Credit (documentary credit) via SWIFT MT700 for bulk orders exceeding USD 50,000, where the Canadian bank issues an irrevocable LC in favor of the overseas supplier, with settlement upon presentation of commercial invoice, packing list, full set of ocean or air waybill bills of lading, sanitary/phytosanitary certificate, and certificate of origin. The partnership should maintain a USD-denominated operating account to pay LC beneficiaries in USD without double conversion. Documentary collection (D/P) via SWIFT MT422 is a permissible fallback for established counterparties. All outbound wires require the supplier's bank account details, accurate beneficiary legal name, and ISIC 4638 trade description; disbursements to high-risk jurisdictions trigger enhanced sanctions screening but do not require pre-approval from the Bank of Canada.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX contracts (settled within two business days) for immediate conversion of USD trade receipts into CAD
Outright FX forwards (vanilla deliverable forwards) with tenors up to 12 months for fixing the CAD/USD or CAD/CNY rate on committed invoices
FX swaps (swap of principal and interest in two currencies on a spot-start or forward-start basis) for temporary liquidity rebalancing

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing CAD against restrictedon-shore currencies, transacted when the underlying trade is denominated in a currency not deliverable offshore (e.g., certain Asia-Pacific receivables)
Cross-currency swaps (fixed-to-floating or floating-to-floating) to match the LP's USD revenue stream against CAD operating costs
Vanilla FX options (purchase of put or call options) to establish a guaranteed floor or cap on conversion rates without removing upside

All hedging instruments must be executed under an ISDA Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex with the tier-1 counterparty bank; the partnership is classified as a commercial end-user eligible for the physical commodity hedging exemption from mandatory central clearing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and Schedule 50 partner allocation schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Partnerships and Trust Accounts Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal-period anniversary rule: due within 5 months after each partnership fiscal period end; a December 31 year-end LP files by May 31; a non-calendar year-end LP files by the last day of the fifth month following the period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: ITA s. 162(7) penalty of CAD 25 per partner per month, capped at 12 months; additional CAD 25 per month per slip penalty for incomplete Schedule 50 data; CRA may issue a demand to file and, for wilful non-compliance, pursue prosecution under ITA s. 238; persistent failure triggers CRA audit and may contribute to provincial administrative strike-off where the provincial annual declaration remains unfiled.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: The Canadian Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent under ITA s.96: no federal corporate income tax is payable at the LP level; each general and limited partner is taxed on its allocated share of partnership income. Reference federal headline rates for partners who are corporations: 15% general corporate rate, reduced to 9% for the first CAD 500,000 of active business income of a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) partner. For individual partners, federal top marginal rate is 33%, producing a combined federal-provincial rate of approximately 44% to 54% depending on province of residence. Non-resident partners are taxable under Part I of the ITA on their share of Canadian-source business income, subject to treaty relief.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sector-specific tax holiday applies to wholesale dehydrated-vegetable and spice trading. Relevant preferential measures for corporate partners: refundable SR&ED investment tax credits (15% general, 35% for small CCPCs on qualifying expenditures); immediate expensing of Canadian manufacturing and processing machinery and equipment acquired before 2028 (Income Tax Regulations s.1100(11)); accelerated CCA Class 43.1/43.2 for qualifying clean-energy assets; Atlantic Investment Tax Credit of 10% in Atlantic provinces. Loss utilization: non-capital losses may be carried back 3 years and forward 20 years; corporate partners' allowable capital losses are carried back 3 years and forward 5 years, and non-resident partners can only use such losses against Canadian-source Part I income.
